component.name: spring-ws
component.title: Spring WebService
component.description: Expose SOAP services, or send requests to SOAP services, using Spring Web Services.
component.label: webservice

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

useGlobalSslContextParameters.label: security
useGlobalSslContextParameters.description: Whether to use the global SSL context parameters of the CamelContext for each endpoint that the component creates and that has no sslContextParameters. The producer uses them for the HTTPS requests that it sends, as described for the sslContextParameters option. The consumer does not use them.

CamelSpringWebserviceEndpointUri.label: producer
CamelSpringWebserviceEndpointUri.description: The address that the producer sends the request to. This header replaces the webServiceEndpointUri option, and the default URI of the WebServiceTemplate of the webServiceTemplate option.

CamelSpringWebserviceSoapAction.label: producer
CamelSpringWebserviceSoapAction.description: The SOAP action of the request that the producer sends. This header replaces the soapAction option.

CamelSpringWebserviceSoapHeader.label: producer
CamelSpringWebserviceSoapHeader.description: The SOAP header as XML. The consumer sets it to the SOAP header of the request, as a javax.xml.transform.Source of the soap:Header element. The producer converts it to a Source and adds the XML to the content of the SOAP header of the request that it sends. When allowResponseHeaderOverride is true, the producer sets it to the SOAP header of the response.

CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingAction.label: producer
CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingAction.description: The WS-Addressing 1.0 Action header of the request that the producer sends. This header replaces the wsAddressingAction option.

CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingFaultTo.label: producer
CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingFaultTo.description: The address of the WS-Addressing FaultTo header of the request that the producer sends. Only used when the wsAddressingAction option or the CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingAction header is set. This header replaces the faultTo option.

CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingReplyTo.label: producer
CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingReplyTo.description: The address of the WS-Addressing ReplyTo header of the request that the producer sends. Only used when the wsAddressingAction option or the CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingAction header is set. This header replaces the replyTo option.

breadcrumbId.label: consumer
breadcrumbId.description: The breadcrumb id of the request. The consumer sets it to the value of the breadcrumbId transport header of the request, for example an HTTP header, when breadcrumb is enabled on the CamelContext.

consumerOut.description: The payload of the SOAP body as a javax.xml.transform.Source (a DOMSource with the default SAAJ message factory); convertBodyTo String gives the XML. The SOAP header is in the CamelSpringWebserviceSoapHeader header

consumerReply.description: The response payload as XML: a String, bytes, a stream cache, a Source or a DOM Document. A body that does not convert to a Source, such as a Map, gives an empty SOAP body without an error

producerIn.description: The request payload as XML: a String, bytes, a stream cache, a Source or a DOM Document. No body, a File, a Map or a number fails: read or marshal it to XML first

producerOut.description: The payload of the SOAP response as a javax.xml.transform.Source (a DOMSource with the default SAAJ message factory), null for an empty SOAP body; also with the InOnly pattern

type.label: consumer
type.description: The endpoint mapping type, which names the part of a request that is compared with lookupKey to select the requests for the consumer. rootqname: the qualified name of the root element of the payload. soapaction: the SOAP action. uri: the URI of the request. uripath: the path of the URI of the request. xpathresult: the result of the XPath expression of the expression option for the request. action: the WS-Addressing Action header. to: the WS-Addressing To header. beanname: no part of the request, because lookupKey names a CamelEndpointDispatcher bean and an existing Spring-WS endpoint mapping maps requests to that bean. The endpoint URI takes the type as written here, without the underscore of the enum constant, and ignores its case.

lookupKey.label: consumer
lookupKey.description: The value that is compared with the part of the request that type names. With rootqname, a QName in the form {namespaceURI}localPart, for example {http://example.com/}GetFoo. With uripath, a value that ends with * matches each path that starts with the text before the *. With action, the WS-Addressing Action can be followed by a colon and the To, and with to, the To can be followed by a colon and the Action. A consumer with such a combined value takes precedence over a consumer with the Action or the To alone. With beanname, the name of a CamelEndpointDispatcher bean in the registry.

webServiceEndpointUri.label: producer
webServiceEndpointUri.description: The address that the producer sends requests to. Written in the path of the endpoint URI in place of type and lookupKey, for example spring-ws:http://foo.com/bar. The CamelSpringWebserviceEndpointUri header replaces this address for a request that the producer sends. Not used when the WebServiceTemplate of the webServiceTemplate option has a default URI.

headerFilterStrategy.label: common
headerFilterStrategy.description: To use a custom HeaderFilterStrategy to filter headers mapped to and from the Camel message. By default the internal Camel and camel header namespace (case-insensitive) is filtered out from inbound SOAP headers, and the default message filter does not write it into outbound SOAP headers.

messageFilter.description: Option to provide a custom MessageFilter. For example when you want to process your headers or attachments by your own.

messageIdStrategy.label: common
messageIdStrategy.description: Option to provide a custom MessageIdStrategy to control generation of WS-Addressing unique message ids.

endpointDispatcher.label: consumer
endpointDispatcher.description: The org.apache.camel.component.spring.ws.bean.CamelEndpointDispatcher that passes requests to the consumer. An existing Spring-WS endpoint mapping, such as a PayloadRootQNameEndpointMapping or a SoapActionEndpointMapping, maps requests to this bean. When type is beanname, the component sets this option to the CamelEndpointDispatcher bean in the registry whose name is lookupKey.

endpointMapping.label: consumer
endpointMapping.description: The org.apache.camel.component.spring.ws.bean.CamelSpringWSEndpointMapping bean that maps requests to the consumer. Required for every type except beanname. Use a CamelEndpointMapping for the types rootqname, soapaction, uri, uripath and xpathresult, and a WSACamelEndpointMapping for the types action and to. The consumer registers itself with the bean when it starts, so one bean can serve all consumers of its types. The MessageDispatcher of Spring-WS must use the same bean, which it does by default for each EndpointMapping bean in its ApplicationContext.

expression.label: consumer
expression.description: The XPath expression to use when option type=xpathresult. Then this option is required to be configured.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

allowResponseAttachmentOverride.label: producer
allowResponseAttachmentOverride.description: Whether to copy the attachments of the response to the Camel message. If true, the producer adds each attachment of the response to the Camel message under its content id, where it replaces an attachment that the Camel message already has under that id.

allowResponseHeaderOverride.label: producer
allowResponseHeaderOverride.description: Whether to copy the SOAP header of the response to the Camel message. If true, the producer sets the CamelSpringWebserviceSoapHeader header to the SOAP header of the response, and sets a Camel header for each attribute and each element of that SOAP header. The name of each of these Camel headers is the local part of the name of the attribute or element, and they replace Camel headers of the same name. The names of the SOAP response header attributes and elements are filtered using the headerFilterStrategy, which by default filters out the internal Camel and camel header namespace (case-insensitive).

faultAction.label: producer
faultAction.description: The WS-Addressing Action header of a SOAP fault that the consumer returns. Only used when endpointMapping is a WSACamelEndpointMapping. If not set, the Action header of the request followed by the faultActionSuffix of the WSACamelEndpointMapping is used, and that suffix is Response by default. The producer does not use it.

faultTo.label: producer
faultTo.description: The address of the WS-Addressing FaultTo header of the request that the producer sends. Only used when the wsAddressingAction option or the CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingAction header is set. The CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingFaultTo header replaces this option for a request that the producer sends.

messageFactory.label: producer
messageFactory.description: Option to provide a custom WebServiceMessageFactory.

messageSender.label: producer
messageSender.description: To use a custom org.springframework.ws.transport.WebServiceMessageSender, for example to perform authentication or to use another transport. The producer sends its requests with it, in place of the message senders of the WebServiceTemplate. With a WSACamelEndpointMapping, Spring-WS sends the response of the consumer with it when the response goes to the WS-Addressing ReplyTo or FaultTo address of the request instead of the connection of the request.

outputAction.label: producer
outputAction.description: The WS-Addressing Action header of the response that the consumer returns. Only used when endpointMapping is a WSACamelEndpointMapping. If not set, the Action header of the request followed by the outputActionSuffix of the WSACamelEndpointMapping is used, and that suffix is Response by default. The producer does not use it.

replyTo.label: producer
replyTo.description: The address of the WS-Addressing ReplyTo header of the request that the producer sends. Only used when the wsAddressingAction option or the CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingAction header is set. The CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingReplyTo header replaces this option for a request that the producer sends.

soapAction.label: producer
soapAction.description: The SOAP action of the request that the producer sends. The CamelSpringWebserviceSoapAction header replaces this option for a request that the producer sends.

timeout.label: producer
timeout.description: The socket read timeout in milliseconds for the requests that the producer sends. Only applied to a message sender of the WebServiceTemplate whose class is exactly HttpUrlConnectionMessageSender, which is the default message sender, or exactly HttpComponentsMessageSender. For any other message sender, the producer logs a warning and does not apply it, so set the timeout on the message sender itself. If not set, the read timeout of the message sender applies. Use 0 for no timeout.

webServiceTemplate.label: producer
webServiceTemplate.description: Option to provide a custom WebServiceTemplate. This allows for full control over client-side web services handling; like adding a custom interceptor or specifying a fault resolver, message sender or message factory.

wsAddressingAction.label: producer
wsAddressingAction.description: The WS-Addressing 1.0 Action header of the request that the producer sends. If set, the producer also adds a MessageID header, a ReplyTo header when replyTo is set, and a FaultTo header when faultTo is set. The CamelSpringWebserviceAddressingAction header replaces this option for a request that the producer sends. If neither is set, the producer adds no WS-Addressing headers.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

sslContextParameters.label: security
sslContextParameters.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.support.jsse.SSLContextParameters for the HTTPS requests that the producer sends. Only applied to a message sender of the WebServiceTemplate whose class is exactly HttpUrlConnectionMessageSender, which is the default message sender. For any other message sender, the producer logs a warning and does not apply it. If not set, the component sets it to the global SSL context parameters when it creates the endpoint and its own useGlobalSslContextParameters option is true. The consumer does not use it.
